Bobowa Jewish Cemetery

Jewish Cemetery · Bobowa, Poland

Not demolished. Jews settled in Bobowa after 1732; the town became a significant Hasidic center in the 19th century, and by 1921, 565 Jews (40%) were mostly murdered at Bełżec in 1942. This cemetery, likely established in the 18th century, served Bobowa and surrounding communities; Szlomo Halberstam, the first Bobover Rebbe, was buried here in 1905. A WWI military section (War Cemetery No. 132) holds 7 Austro-Hungarian Jewish soldiers who died 1914-1915. During WWII, this cemetery became a direct execution site - about 17 people shot on January 5, 1942, and 30 more on March 4, 1942. Poland formally closed the cemetery in 1961. The Nissenbaum Family Foundation cleaned, fenced, and memorialized the mass grave in 1988; a modern ohel now shelters both Szlomo Halberstam and his son-in-law Chaim Jakow Teitelbaum.
